newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker but underpinned by 899.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends weaker but underpinned by 899.

text.p: Left-over origin sales weighed on London cocoa futures in their last session before the Christmas break on Tuesday but traders noted underlying support.

Helped by a lower opening call, the key second-month March position dipped to its sensitive contract low of 899 stg a tonne for the second time since last week. It quickly recovered to close at the well-worn 900 stg level, down three on the day.
Other contracts lost between two and five stg and the volume totalled 2,390 lots.

Trading at the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE) will resume on Friday December 27 but volume is expected to be thin with most players extending their Christmas break to a long weekend.
Traders said sterling's strength against the dollar and steady Ivorian arrivals seemed to have pressured the market in Tuesday's short session.
"Some people are viewing the Ivorian arrivals quite high compared to expectations," said one.
He was referring to the latest estimates by the U.S.-based General Cocoa which put Ivorian arrivals at 435,000 tonnes up to December 14, against 545,000 tonnes at the same time last year.
In a weekly newsletter dated December 20, General Cocoa said the estimate was some 50,000 tonnes higher than previously thought and that the total was likely to exceed 1.0 million tonnes.
Other projections for the Ivorian 1996/97 crop range between 850,000 and 1.0 million tonnes.
Technically, March faces overhead supply between 916 and 930 stg and a major downtrendline dating from August at 940.
Selling by Ivory Coast dragged values lower on Monday but traders expected another bottom forming at 899 stg basis March.
